- When sentiment shows a sharp upward spike followed by a drop, model tends to overreact and overshoot — correct by reducing forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative or flat over 3+ days, model underestimates downward pressure — adjust forecast downward by 2–5%.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 2–3 days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% per day.
- In high-news-volume periods, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each 3+ news unit.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.67+ change over 2 days), model exhibits mean reversion bias — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is rising in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
